title: Support downlit-style auto-linking for R function and package references
description: The [downlit](https://downlit.r-lib.org/) R package auto-links package and function references in rendered R content. Two flavors: 1. **Code-block autolinks** — function names inside R code blocks become hyperlinks to their docs (rdrr.io for base R / CRAN packages, pkgdown sites for tidyverse-style packages). Example: ```html install.packages("bslib") ``` 2. **Prose autolinks** — bare-word mentions of "attached" packages in prose link to the package homepage. Triggered by an `options(download.attached = c("shiny", "bslib"))` chunk in the source `.qmd`. Example: every plain-text `bslib` mention becomes `bslib`. The current Hugo site renders neither flavor. Supporting them would benefit ported posts (authored expecting downlit) and any new R-content posts. ## Ported posts where downlit-generated links are missing | Post | Local | Legacy | |---|---|---| | bslib-dashboards | [opensource.posit.co](https://opensource.posit.co/blog/2023-06-07_bslib-dashboards/) | [shiny.posit.co](https://shiny.posit.co/blog/posts/bslib-dashboards/) | | bslib-tooltips | [opensource.posit.co](https://opensource.posit.co/blog/2023-08-16_bslib-tooltips/) | [shiny.posit.co](https://shiny.posit.co/blog/posts/bslib-tooltips/) | | shiny-r-1.8.0 | [opensource.posit.co](https://opensource.posit.co/blog/2023-11-30_shiny-r-1.8.0/) | [shiny.posit.co](https://shiny.posit.co/blog/posts/shiny-r-1.8.0/) | | shiny-r-1.8.1 | [opensource.posit.co](https://opensource.posit.co/blog/2024-03-27_shiny-r-1.8.1/) | [shiny.posit.co](https://shiny.posit.co/blog/posts/shiny-r-1.8.1/) |

title: Support `.code-overflow-wrap` class on code blocks
description:
## Problem

By default, code cells in blog posts get a horizontal-scroll treatment when their content exceeds the column width. For short single-line entries (e.g. a one-line shell command, a YAML key) this produces an awkward narrow scrollable strip when the content would actually fit if simply wrapped.

Quarto's HTML format supports the `code-overflow-wrap` option (and a corresponding `.code-overflow-wrap` class) that flips a code block to `white-space: pre-wrap` so it wraps instead of scrolling. We don't currently honour that class on this site.

## Proposal

Add a CSS rule so that any code block (or its container) carrying the `code-overflow-wrap` class wraps:

```css
.code-overflow-wrap pre,
pre.code-overflow-wrap,
pre code.code-overflow-wrap {
  white-space: pre-wrap;
  word-break: break-word;
}
```

That lets authors opt in per block via Quarto's existing syntax (`{.code-overflow-wrap}` on a fence, or `code-overflow: wrap` in the cell options) without changing the default behaviour for code that's genuinely meant to scroll (e.g. wide shell output).

## Posts that would benefit

These ported Quarto posts have at least one code cell where wrap would read better than scroll:

- `content/blog/quarto/2024-01-24-1.4-release/`
- `content/blog/quarto/2024-12-12-includes-meta/`
- `content/blog/quarto/2025-10-20-quarto-wizard-1-0-0/`

Surfaced during the Quarto-blog port review.

title: Code block copy buttons have no accessible name
description:
## What

axe-core flags a **critical** `button-name` violation on every blog post that contains a code block. The copy-to-clipboard button rendered into each code block has no accessible name — no inner text, no `aria-label`, no `title`. Screen readers will announce it as "button" with no indication of what it does.

Rule: [`button-name`](https://dequeuniversity.com/rules/axe/4.11/button-name) — *Buttons must have discernible text*

## Where

The button is emitted by a layout/partial (or render hook) that decorates `.code-block .highlight`. It appears on every post with one or more code blocks, so this is a layout-level fix, not a per-post one.

Offending HTML:

```html
<button class="right-1 top-1 absolute" type="button">
```

## Suggested fix

Add an accessible name to the button in whichever partial renders it — e.g. `aria-label="Copy code"`, or a visually-hidden span with text. An SVG icon child should also have `aria-hidden="true"` so its title doesn't get announced separately.

| Land on `/blog/?topics=ai`, then clear the filter | stays hidden |

Featured visibility is decided once at page load and never updates when filters change. It should track the filter state in real time — visible when no filters are active, hidden when any are.

Surfaced while reviewing #178.

title: Pagefind search is eagerly loading all results
description:
Heya — just floating that the Pagefind search implementation here feels a bit slower than it otherwise could, mainly as the data for all results is loaded up front. If you peep the network tab during a search, the fragments for all results have to load first which slows things down.

The best strategy is to lazy load the data for each result on scroll using an IntersectionObserver, if at all possible, so that only the visible results load their data at any given time :) _(nb: 1.5 is also just blanket faster but that's tangential)_. 

If this is the sorta thing you'd toss an agent at, the new [pagefind-results.ts component](https://github.com/Pagefind/pagefind/blob/main/pagefind_ui/component/components/pagefind-results.ts) has all the patterns one would want to replicate for a snappier feel.

title: Create Hugo shortcodes for tabsets, callouts, and code filenames
description:
Tabsets, callouts, and code filenames are currently implemented as Quarto Lua filters that emit HTML and CSS directly. This means they only work in `.qmd` posts.

To support these features in `.md` posts too, each should follow the same pattern used for videos:

1. **Create a Hugo shortcode** that owns the rendering logic (HTML + CSS)
2. **Simplify the Lua filter** to just translate Quarto's native syntax into calls to the shortcode

This gives `.md` authors access to these features via shortcode syntax, while `.qmd` authors keep using the native Quarto syntax they already know.

### Features

- **Tabsets** — Quarto's `::: {.panel-tabset}` → `{{</* tabset */>}}` shortcode
- **Callouts** — Quarto's `::: {.callout-note}` etc. → `{{</* callout */>}}` shortcode
- **Code filenames** — Quarto's `{filename="doc.qmd"}` → shortcode or render hook that adds a filename label

### Related

- #134 — Style filename labels on code blocks

title: Unify image alt text and caption syntax across .qmd and .md posts
description:
Currently, authors need to remember different syntax for alt text and captions depending on whether they're writing a `.qmd` or `.md` post:

### `.qmd` posts

Alt text uses the `fig-alt` attribute, caption goes in `[]`:

```markdown
![Caption](image.png){fig-alt="Alt text"}
```

But `fig-alt` renders to `data-fig-alt` in the hugo-md output — not to `alt` — so the alt text is lost for screen readers. ([Tracked upstream](https://github.com/quarto-dev/quarto-cli/issues/14344))

### `.md` posts

Alt text goes in `[]`, caption uses a title string:

```markdown
![Alt text](image.png "Caption")
```

### Ideal state

Authors shouldn't need to think about which format they're in. We should find a way to make image accessibility and captions work consistently across both formats — ideally with a single syntax, or at minimum with a render hook or shortcode that normalises the output.

title: Replace Quarto's table-based layouts with CSS grid filter
description:
Quarto's `layout-ncol` / `layout-nrow` divs get converted to HTML `<table>` elements. This causes two problems:

1. **Markdown inside cells doesn't parse.** Goldmark treats content inside `<td>` as raw HTML, so markdown code fences (including those with `filename` attributes from the code-filename filter) silently disappear.

2. **Layout tables aren't semantic.** Screen readers may announce these as data tables.

A Lua filter using the same HTML+AST sandwich pattern as `callout.lua` and `tabset.lua` could intercept layout divs at `pre-ast` and emit something more appropriate. Need to decide if this is best handled by adding `div`s and CSS classes, or using something like a Hugo shortcode.

### Posts currently affected

- `content/blog/quarto/2025-07-24-parameterized-reports-python/index.qmd` — 2 code blocks with `filename` inside `layout-ncol="2"`
- `content/blog/quarto/2025-10-20-quarto-wizard-1-0-0/index.qmd` — 2 code blocks with `filename` inside `layout-ncol="2"`

These were intentionally left unrendered in #128 to avoid losing content.

title: Software ordering
description: Currently, software ordering is done by the repo's stars. I've made drive-by PRs to the top 6 repos. They do not represent _me_. ------------------ I'm inclined to request that some sort of priority queue be created. Maybe... * Number of commits that I own to the main branch * Percentage of commits that I own to the main branch * Packages where I'm the maintainer first, tie-breaker to another method ? ------------------- From Claude: ``` How would you rank GitHub repos within a website given every GitHub repo that I've contributed to? I do not want to overemphasize small contributions to repos with large amount of stars. ``` -------------------- > ## Ranking GitHub Repos by Contribution > > The core challenge is balancing **contribution depth** vs **repo popularity** without letting > one dominate. Here's a framework: > > --- > > ### The Problem with Naive Approaches > > | Approach | Problem | > |---|---| > | Sort by stars | 1 commit to linux/linux ranks #1 | > | Sort by commit count | Your personal toy repos dominate | > | Multiply contributions × stars | Same star problem, just scaled | > > --- > > ### Recommended: Geometric Mean with Log-Scaled Popularity > > score = contribution_depth^α × log(1 + stars)^β > > Where `α > β` (e.g., α=0.7, β=0.3) to weight contribution more heavily. > > **Why geometric mean?** It naturally penalizes imbalance — a near-zero contribution score keeps > the total score low regardless of star count. Additive methods don't have this property. > > **Why `log(stars)`?** Compresses the 1M-star vs 1K-star gap from 1000x to ~2x. > > --- > > ### Contribution Depth Score > > Build a composite from available signals, normalized to [0, 1]: > > ``` > contribution_depth = > (commits_by_you / total_commits) * 0.4 + > (prs_merged_by_you / total_prs) * 0.35 + > (reviews_given / total_reviews) * 0.15 + > (issues_opened / total_issues) * 0.10 > ``` > > Commits and merged PRs carry the most weight since they represent substantive work. > > --- > > ### Recency Decay (optional) > > Repos you're actively contributing to should rank higher than old ones: > > ``` > decay = e^(-λ × years_since_last_contribution) > ``` > > A `λ` of ~0.3 gives roughly half-weight to contributions 2+ years old. > > --- > > ### Full Formula > > ``` > score = contribution_depth^0.7 × log(1 + stars)^0.3 × decay > ``` > > --- > > ### Practical Tiebreakers > > When scores are close, break ties by: > 1. Whether you're an **owner or maintainer** (hard boost) > 2. Whether the repo is **currently active** (recent commits in last 6 months) > 3. **Fork count** as a secondary popularity signal (more signal-diverse than stars alone) > > --- > > ### What to Avoid > > - **Raw star count** as a linear factor > - **Commit count** without normalizing against total repo commits > - Giving credit for being added as a contributor with 1 commit to a 50K-star repo — this should > score near the bottom > > The geometric mean approach handles the edge cases cleanly without needing arbitrary thresholds > or special-case logic.

title: Investigate Hugo image processing memory issues for blog content
description: ## Background During the blog porting work (#22 ), we discovered that Hugo's WASM-based image processor crashes with memory allocation errors when processing large numbers of images at once. The site has ~16,000 images across ~1,000 blog posts. ## Current workaround We disabled responsive image processing (WebP + srcsets) specifically for blog content in two templates: | File | Change | Reason | |------|--------|--------| | `layouts/partials/item.html` | Skip `responsive_image_container.html` when `$is_blog` | Blog list pages render many thumbnails at once | | `layouts/_default/_markup/render-image.html` | Simple `` for blog section | Blog posts contain many markdown images | Blog hero images and related post thumbnails still get full responsive/WebP processing — these render one post at a time, not in bulk. Non-blog content (software, events, resources, people) retains full image processing. ## Error details When processing too many images, Hugo produces errors like: ``` Error allocating memory for blob data Error parsing JSON line panic: call with ID 0 not found ``` This appears to be related to Hugo's WASM-based WebP processing (`github.com/gohugoio/hugo/internal/warpc`). ## Things to investigate - [ ] Is this a known Hugo issue? Check hugo GitHub issues for WASM memory problems - [ ] Does Hugo have configuration options to limit concurrent image processing or increase memory? - [ ] Would upgrading Hugo versions help? (Current: check `hugo version`) - [ ] Could we process images in smaller batches somehow? - [ ] Is the issue specifically WebP, or does JPEG srcset processing also contribute? - [ ] Would pre-processing blog images (outside Hugo) be a viable alternative? ## Testing approach To reproduce, restore main's version of `item.html` and run `hugo`: ```bash git stash git checkout main -- layouts/partials/item.html hugo # Will crash with memory errors git checkout HEAD -- layouts/partials/item.html git stash pop ```

title: Add `software` and `languages` taxonomies to ported blog posts
description:
Ported blog posts are missing the `software` and `languages` taxonomies, which are needed for cross-linking with other site content.

## Context

These taxonomies connect blog posts to:
- `/software/{name}/` pages (e.g., plotnine, shiny-r, quarto)
- `/languages/{name}/` pages (e.g., python, r)

## Current state

Most ported posts have `ported_from` set but lack `software` and `languages` in their frontmatter.

## Proposed approach

For each post, add:

```yaml
software:
  - package-name  # match folder names in content/software/
languages:
  - python        # or r, or both
```

### Mapping from `ported_from`

Some mappings are straightforward:
| `ported_from` | Likely `software` | Likely `languages` |
|---------------|-------------------|-------------------|
| plotnine | plotnine | python |
| great_tables | great-tables | python (and/or r) |
| shiny | shiny-r and/or shiny-python | r and/or python |
| pointblank | pointblank | python (and/or r) |
| quarto | quarto | (varies) |
| tidyverse | (various) | r |
| positron | positron | (varies) |

Posts will need individual review — many cover multiple packages or languages.

title: Cull RStudio blog posts
description:
The `content/blog/rstudio/` folder contains ~400 posts ported from the old RStudio blog. Many of these are about commercial products and don't belong on the open-source website.

## Posts to EXCLUDE

Posts primarily about commercial/enterprise products:
- **RStudio Connect** (`rstudio-connect-*`) — ~50+ posts
- **RStudio Server Pro / Workbench** (`rstudio-server-pro-*`, `rstudio-workbench-*`)
- **RStudio Package Manager** (`rstudio-package-manager-*`)
- **Shiny Server Pro** (`shiny-server-pro-*`)
- **Professional Drivers** (`professional-drivers-*`)
- **RStudio Desktop Pro** (commercial license version)
- Enterprise thought leadership / marketing interviews
- Workshop registration / training promotion posts

## Posts to KEEP

- Open-source package releases (tidyverse, shiny, keras, sparklyr, etc.)
- Open-source RStudio IDE releases (non-Pro features)
- Technical tutorials using open-source tools
- Internship announcements (work on open-source projects)
- Community announcements related to open-source

## Gray areas

- RStudio IDE posts that mix open-source and Pro features
- Conference talk recordings (keep if focused on open-source tools)

## Suggested approach

1. Create exclusion list based on folder name patterns
2. Manual review of ~50 edge cases
3. Either delete excluded posts or move to a separate archive

title: CI does not fail on Hugo build warnings or a degraded search index
description:
## Problem

The `build-and-deploy` job treats Hugo warnings as noise. Nothing inspects them, so broken references scroll past in the log and deploy to production unnoticed.

This is not hypothetical. A local build with the Hugo version CI pins (extended 0.158.0) produced **4 warnings**, all live on the useR! 2026 event page at the time of filing:

```
WARN  item partial: page not found for slug 'blog/2026-07-14_user-2026-warsaw/'
WARN  gallery: could not find image "photos/user1.jpg" in page events/user-2026/_index.md
WARN  gallery: could not find image "photos/user2.jpg" in page events/user-2026/_index.md
WARN  gallery: could not find image "photos/scipy3.jpeg" in page events/user-2026/_index.md
```

That is a dead card link and three broken images shipped to visitors. CI was green throughout.

## Second, related gap: search index

`yarn build-search` (Pagefind) only exits non-zero when it indexes *nothing at all*. A **partial** index exits 0 and silently ships degraded search.

This is a real risk in this repo specifically, because `data-pagefind-body` is a **site-wide opt-in switch**: once any page carries it, only pages carrying it get indexed. It appears in six layouts:

- `layouts/blog/single.html`
- `layouts/resources/term.html`
- `layouts/software/term.html`
- `layouts/people/term.html`
- `layouts/events/term.html`
- `layouts/_default/single.html`

Drop that attribute from `layouts/blog/single.html` during a refactor and ~1,048 blog posts disappear from search. Hugo emits no warning, Pagefind exits 0, and CI stays green. Current index size is 3,235 pages.

## Proposed fix

Add two asserts to `build-deploy.yml`, both **before** the Netlify step so a bad build is never published rather than flagged after it is already live:

1. Tee the Hugo build to a log and fail on any `WARN`/`ERROR` line, with an allowlist file for warnings that genuinely cannot be fixed.
2. Assert the Pagefind page count against a floor set just under the measured count, so losing any one indexed section trips it.

Since `build-deploy.yml` is `workflow_call`, both gates would cover preview and production deploys.

## Notes / limitations

- A page-count floor cannot catch the small sections (`people` ~59, `events` ~35) disappearing. It is a guard against whole-section regressions, not a per-page ratchet.
- A warnings gate means a new warning blocks a production deploy. The allowlist is the escape hatch.

title: Search hits don't appear in visible card excerpts
description: Searching returns hits whose matched term isn't visible anywhere on the result card. The search index appears to run against full post content, while card excerpts are truncated to a fixed length. If a match occurs past that cutoff, the search still finds it, but the rendered excerpt never shows it. Leaving unverifiable hits. Steps to reproduce: 1. Go to https://opensource.posit.co/people/hadley-wickham/ 2. Search "elevators" 3. Results appear, but no card's visible title/excerpt contains the word
